description: Item #77 (2026-10-07): free-tier-first providers for /ask only (scope router + answer). Tried in order; an entry whose api_key_env is unset is skipped; OpenAI (config/model-selection.json, priced from config/model-pricing.json) is the last resort ONLY when openai_fallback.enabled is true (shipped false). Evaluation paths (TRACE capture, M6 baseline and judge, Gate A, pipeline) never read this file and stay on the selected OpenAI model.

openai_fallback.note: G7 option (b), 2026-10-21: false = the /ask API process never makes an OpenAI call and does not need OPENAI_API_KEY (chain and claim checkers are Groq-only; the default OpenAI client is blocked at runtime). true restores the OpenAI last-resort entry and checker, needs a valid key, and is a reviewed config change plus deploy. Missing block, missing key, non-boolean or unreadable file means off. No env override. Eval and script paths do not read this file.

grace.note: OD-1031-EXHAUST-GRACE (owner 2026-10-31): the exhaustion stop applies to a FRESH prompt (nothing started: legacy 429 / stream 503 'unavailable', never paid inference). When every free provider is exhausted AFTER work has started on an active Ask, no further free-provider calls are made and the response is completed with what exists. openai_completion: true = the steps that still need inference (answer writer, claim check) may use the OpenAI model (config/model-selection.json, priced from config/model-pricing.json; needs OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment) for THIS completion only; the verification standard is unchanged (the draft still goes through the claim check) and the existing per-client and per-day cost caps stay the safety net. Free first, paid only as the recorded fallback (owner rule). It does NOT change openai_fallback.enabled, so fresh prompts never use OpenAI. false, a missing or non-boolean value, a missing key, or an OpenAI failure = the completion is the non-LLM reading list (or the correct no-answer text when nothing was found). DEFAULT ON per owner addendum; value is a decision, not a calibrated threshold.
grace.notice_openai: Note: VERA-DAR was very busy while preparing this answer, so your question, the passages found and the draft answer were sent to OpenAI to finish it. The answer was still checked against its sources as usual.
grace.notice_fallback: Note: VERA-DAR was too busy to write and check an answer just now, so it is showing what it had gathered so far.

exhaustion.note: STREAM-1031 / OD-1031-TOKENS (owner: token use is rate limited by providers; no app-side token caps; when every provider is exhausted, active token-using processes stop). recheck_s is the wait before one probe when a 429/quota error carries no numeric Retry-After header (the header wins when present). PROVISIONAL prior, UNCALIBRATED: no measured Groq 429 recovery distribution yet. Would change on: logged Retry-After values showing a different typical reset (per-minute vs per-day limits), or probes that keep failing (raise) or recover far sooner (lower). State is process-local (accepted divergence, plan s3.7 item 5).

providers.note: Free tier: $0 recorded (Groq's paid rate is listed at $0.075 in / $0.30 out per 1M). reasoning_effort low is required: without it the router's 60-token JSON call fails with 400 json_validate_failed (measured 2026-10-07).
Second Groq model: separate per-model free limits. Same reasoning_effort rule (measured 2026-10-07).

openrouter_example.note: Not active. To add OpenRouter, copy this object into providers (OpenAI stays the implied last resort), set model to a current ':free' id from https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, and set OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Free models allow 50 requests/day without purchased credits (1,000/day with $10+). Check the account's privacy settings first: some providers may log or train on prompts.

grounding.note: Item #79 (2026-10-07): /ask searches these providers once per accepted question (and, when scope_router.json offtopic_reading_list is true, once with the scholarly-only providers arxiv and openalex for a layer-2 out-of-scope question; with domain routing on that is up to 1 + 2 queries (question plus domain terms, max_domain_branches), still scholarly-only, with link following off and no stored branch). Results with an abstract are used directly; link-only results (DuckDuckGo, news, portals, OpenAlex records without an abstract) are followed to their original scholarly sources under `resolve` (vera/source_resolver.py). Only sources with an abstract reach the grounded-v1 prompt (vera/trace_eval/capture.py).
grounding._arxiv_off_note: CONTROL-GAPS-1107 ARXIV-OFF: off because export.arxiv.org robots.txt disallows / for all agents and arxiv.org disallows /api; interim until the owner decides (H-1). grounding.providers still lists "arxiv" but only filters the chain; the chain itself skips arXiv via vera_eval_run.json search.arxiv.enabled=false.
grounding.no_sources_text: VERA-DAR could not find published sources for this question right now, so it has not answered from memory. Please try again shortly or rephrase the question.
grounding.removed_citation_note: Note: citation markers that did not match a listed source were removed.
grounding.insufficient_text: VERA-DAR found sources for this question, but its answer did not contain a claim it could tie to them, so it has not answered. The sources it found are listed below; please read them directly or rephrase.

claim_check.note: Item #79 (R1 criterion: each cited claim is checked against the cited record's text). One call per answer judges every cited sentence against the abstracts it cites. Checkers are tried in order; a different model family from the answering model is preferred. If every checker fails, the answer fails closed to unavailable_text.
claim_check.context_title_note: FA8-2 (IMPL-1028-FA8). UNCALIBRATED. true: each cited passage is sent to the checker as {title, text} and the rubric gains 'a claim attributed to a different subject, population or activity than the passage describes is unsupported'. Titles are capped at 300 characters (TITLE_MAX_CHARS, UNCALIBRATED). Default false = prompt unchanged. This block also feeds the abstract path (ask_service.py:842-849), so both switches change abstract answers too, not only full-document/D8. Calibrate before enabling: run the checker before/after on at least 60 hand-labelled live (claim, passage) pairs (F-4 close set in gates-1029 plus the 4 live-check answers), two skeptic agents on distinct models label the pairs, record the verdict-transition matrix and false-pass / false-drop counts (plan-1028-firstask section 6). Owner flips.
claim_check.keep_partial_note: FA8-3 (IMPL-1028-FA8). UNCALIBRATED. true (default) = today's behaviour: partial claims are kept and marked. false = partial claims are removed like unsupported ones (counted in 'removed', record verdict stays 'partial' with partial_removed=true) and the per-part D8 coverage recomputes from the supported claims left. Calibrate with the same at-least-60-pair before/after run as context_title (false-drop count of genuinely adequate partial claims vs false-pass count removed). Owner decision OD-FA-8.

checkers.json_mode_note: A2 (2026-10-21, Groq 400 hypothesis H2, unconfirmed): no response_format for this checker; the fail-closed _parse rejects a non-JSON reply and the next checker runs. qwen3 may emit <think> text here, so expect an extra check call before gpt-oss; uncalibrated, to be measured in G7.

claim_check.removed_note: Note: sentences the cited abstracts did not support were removed.
claim_check.unavailable_text: VERA-DAR could not verify its draft answer against the sources right now, so it has not answered. The sources it found are listed below.

corpus.note: Item #79 phase C (R1 2026-10-07: full Gate A scoring). After each grounded /ask, sources with abstracts go through Gate A then the licence gate; every candidate is recorded with its decision, and fetch+allowed ones are stored as corpus sources (metadata and abstract only). Runs after the response. Uses the production write-only account; its URL is read from the env var named in db_url_env (unset = disabled). The visitor's question is never stored.
corpus.question_text: VERA /ask corpus accumulation (sources admitted by Gate A and the licence gate; visitor questions are not stored)

corpus_description.note: Item #83 (ported from AI-Internship #80): a model-written description of VERA-DAR's own corpus (vera_vjay.sources), from titles and provenance metadata only, regenerated only when the source count, newest created_at or prompt_version change. Read with the read-only account (URL in the env var named read_db_url_env; unset = not connected). Cached in memory; on model failure a deterministic description is served and generation retries after retry_s (echo_retry_s after a generated text that reproduced a source title; code fallback 3600 when absent).
corpus_description.note_digest_1104: CORPUS-DIGEST-1104: agentic digest (vera/corpus_description.py run_digest_pipeline): cluster, draft, check; at most 3 model calls over the /ask chain (free providers first). agentic.* are work bounds (time, tokens, caps), not decision thresholds. sample_excerpt_chars 0 = titles only (abstract excerpts are not sent; a value above 0 needs an owner decision). Failure keeps the previous digest in memory, else the deterministic description. Supersedes the one-shot description in note above.

stored_taxonomy._note: WP6 (CHUNK-TAXO-WP6-1109): true shows the stored per-chunk taxonomy labels (domains, topics, subtopics; document vote and union of chunks) on the Corpus Description page and in /corpus-summary (key stored_taxonomy). Default false = the interim page, unchanged. The block also needs the in-app job's mechanical display gate to have passed (vera.chunk_taxo_status.status() display_ok); otherwise the interim page stands. Turn on only per the owner's decision D3.

subject_names._note: SUBJECT-BUILD-1114 WP-S4 (vera/subject_names.py): false = no model-written node names. true (also needs corpus_description.answer_subject.enabled true, stored_taxonomy.enabled true and the display gate open) lets a bounded background warm-up name each existing taxonomy node over the free-tier /ask chain, in memory only, one attempt per node per job version per process. max_calls_per_version is a work bound (cost cap on the shared free chain), not a decision threshold; beyond it the term label is shown.

unlabelled_share._note: CORPUS-UNCAT-1113: true shows, on the Corpus Description page and in /corpus-summary (key unlabelled), how many documents and stored passages have no stored subject label (read-only aggregate of the migration-020 tables; no external call). Missing or not exactly true = off.

subject_areas._enabled_note: CORPUS-INTERIM-1108 (owner 2026-11-08): false hides per-subject counts, shares, assignments and the list of subject areas on the Corpus Description page and sidebar (API and UI both read this switch); the page shows the checked description plus count and year range, or frequent subject phrases (config/corpus_frequent_subjects.json). Set true only once a validated matcher ships; this restores the previous view.
subject_areas._chunk_votes_note: TAXO-INDUCE-1107, PROVISIONAL: each document's topic is the chunk vote (vera/chunk_topics.py) over at most chunks_per_doc evenly spread stored chunks of chunk_chars each (work bounds), else the stored acquisition key, else the title + window match. min_chunk_votes 1 is an uncalibrated prior: one chunk at or above the BM25 acceptance value assigns the document. Calibrate with the owner-run induction dry run (work/TAXO-INDUCE-1107/scripts/run_induction.sh --no-llm reports the not-matched share now) and a spot check; raise min_chunk_votes if single-chunk matches prove wrong. TAXO-MATCH-FIX-1108 (PROVISIONAL, classifier version 2): min_chunk_votes 1 is now only a floor; the document also needs votes from min_vote_share (0.25) of its sampled chunks, and each chunk must pass the strict match rules (generic terms excluded, >= 2 distinct non-generic shared terms, lead over the best other subject area); values and their calibration note are in config/chunk_topic_terms.json. A document whose chunks were read gets no document-level second try. The page prints the exact not-matched count (N of M documents).
subject_areas._calibration_note: CORPUS-DESC-1107, PROVISIONAL (not calibrated on real data; the implementer had no DB read). display_* only bound how many names are listed (the rest is summed into 'other'); scan_max is a work bound (the corpus held about 314 sources on 2026-11-07); connect_timeout_s and statement_timeout_ms are safety bounds. Each document's topic uses the BM25 threshold read from config/auto_acquire.json micro_topic.count_min_score.anchor_bm25.scholarly (2.0, itself a PROVISIONAL prior). Calibration pending the owner-run count (work/CORPUS-COUNTS-OWNER-1107): matched share and spot-checked assignments on real vera_vjay.sources rows; change the threshold or the registry if the unmatched share is high or assignments are wrong.

memory.note: Item #84 write gate (vera/memory_gate.py): structural filter thresholds and lists. Detector lists ported from AI-Internship intake_detectors.json. Not a security guarantee. calibration note: the owner's private planning notes (not published) (statuses PROVISIONAL/UNCALIBRATED; D-038 ACCEPTED by R1 (RD-3) to 2026-10-25 or 20 owner-confirmed rows; values PROVISIONAL/UNCALIBRATED).
memory._discovery_providers_note: MEMPROV-1113: allowed_providers is the evidence-write list and is empty (portal providers arxiv and openalex are not evidence on their label; OD-1110-ARXIV-PORTAL, OD-1110-OPENALEX-PORTAL, OD-1110-PORTALS-ALL). discovery_allowed_providers lists the labels whose search candidates may be named in a discovery note (not evidence).

store.note: Item #84 storage/recall. One fixed question_text for every memory row (visitor questions are never stored). Forgetting: ttl_days + recency decay (half_life_days) at read time; tombstone via claims.detailed_status. Write account URL in db_url_wo_env, read account in db_url_ro_env. Thresholds ttl_days, half_life_days, min_rank, min_matched_terms, max_query_terms, recall_k, max_writes_*: calibration note: the owner's private planning notes (not published) (statuses PROVISIONAL/UNCALIBRATED; D-038 ACCEPTED by R1 (RD-3) to 2026-10-25 or 20 owner-confirmed rows; values PROVISIONAL/UNCALIBRATED).
store.question_text: VERA durable memory: claim-checked, gate-passed findings from corpus sources (trust=tool-derived,claim-checked,auto)
store.confirm_note: D6 (2026-10-10): rows from /ask are written as status_pending and are never recalled; only the operator (owner_key_env, X-Owner-Key) confirms (-> status_live) or rejects (-> status_rejected). status_legacy_auto rows were auto-written before D6; they are not recalled and are listed for review. max_pending is provisional (calibration note: item-84 plan s20).
